articles.title: Gravity, damping and friction
articles.summary: The SDK documents world gravity, vehicle damping and surface friction. The game runs a Bullet world with gravity (0, -10, 0) m/s², fixed solver substeps, damping (1 - d)^dt and contact friction clamp(μA × μB, -10, 10).
articles.body: The SDK gives gravity as 10.0, linear and angular damping as 0.1, and surface friction as 0.8. Its linear damping comment says the value tends toward zero with atmospheric height. These are SDK defaults and configuration entries, not measurements of the running simulation. A native decode (investigation/wheels.md, shown on the Wheels parts pages) found that the game builds a Bullet btSoftRigidDynamicsWorld with a btSequentialImpulseConstraintSolver and sets world gravity to (0, -10, 0) m/s², with Y up. The game_constants binder reads gravity, vehicle_linear_damping, vehicle_angular_damping and vehicle_friction by name, with built-in defaults 10, 0.1, 0.1 and 0.8, and each vehicle passes its configured gravity to its bodies. Projectiles do not use the world gravity: their own integration applies 30 m/s² (investigation/weapons.md). Time steps are fixed (investigation/update-rate.md). Components update 60 times per simulated second; the solver accumulates elapsed time and runs whole substeps of 1/60, 1/120 or 1/180 s, from the 60, 120 or 180 Hz setting, at most 1000 per tick, keeping the remainder for the next tick. Each solver step multiplies a body's linear and angular velocity by (1 - d)^dt, with d clamped to 0 to 1, so the default 0.1 keeps 0.9 of the speed per simulated second at every solver rate. The vehicle body build multiplies the linear damping by (1 - 0.0000224138 × y)^5.3595 below a transformed height y of 40000 and uses 0 above it, which matches the SDK comment (inference: y is the height in metres). Contact friction combines the two bodies' coefficients as clamp(μA × μB, -10, 10) and restitution as their product, so vehicle on vehicle at the default 0.8 gives 0.64. Bullet's own construction default is 0.5. Wheels add a sphere body with friction 0.001 but take their grip from a separate ray request (see Wheels, grip and suspension).

articles.title: Air drag and lift tuning
articles.summary: Hull air drag and lift read built-in game_constants defaults, including air density 1.225. The executable never reads calculate_air_density, so the realtime 0 switches nothing off.
articles.body: The SDK describes linear and quadratic speed factors for pressure and suction drag. The SDK labels 15 m/s as the aerodynamic-force threshold and 50 m/s as the high-speed scaling threshold. A scale of 8 is described as additive. A native decode (investigation/config.md) found where the hull air path reads these values. The vehicle buoyancy and drag routine 0x14048ad30 reads the pressure and suction drag factors 0.05, 0.1, 0.025 and 0.05, the falloff powers 0.6 and 0.4, air_drag_factor 0.2, the three speed settings and air_density from the native constants block. The hull air callback 0x14048e2d0 reads viscous_air_resistance 0.25 and lift_force 0.25. The game sets these constants itself and overrides them only from rom/data/game_constants.xml, which this installation does not ship, so the built-in values apply: air density 1.225, and the same drag and threshold numbers as the SDK. The name calculate_air_density does not occur in the executable as ASCII or UTF-16LE text. The realtime file that sets it to 0 is parsed into a registry that no recovered gameplay code reads. So the 0 does not set a vacuum, switch off air density or disable altitude effects. The realtime file also lists matching drag and threshold values; the hull path reads the native block, not those entries. A separate native decode of the wing, control-surface and fin air routine (investigation/control-surfaces.md, shown on the Control surfaces parts page) found that it multiplies by its own constant 24 and never reads lift_force, so the SDK description of lift_force as surface lift scaling does not hold for those parts. That routine applies an altitude pressure ratio without checking calculate_air_density. The only recovered lift_force read is in the hull air callback.

articles.title: Buoyancy and water drag
articles.summary: Buoyancy pushes up with water_density × g × V ÷ D, where D rises from 10 to 20 as body mass goes from 2000 to 25000. The unmodified game uses the built-in multiplier 10; the realtime file's 12 has no recovered reader.
articles.body: The SDK documents water density as 1000 and exposes separate pressure, suction, viscous and wave-slamming terms. A native decode (investigation/config.md) recovered the buoyancy routine 0x14048ad30 and its water surface callback 0x14048d4d0. Buoyancy: each body gets an upward force water_density × g × V ÷ D. m is the body mass, g its gravity scalar and V a submerged weight summed over an eight-child spatial tree of the body; a partly submerged leaf counts clamp((h - y + r) ÷ 2r, 0, 1) of its weight, h being the sampled water height, y the node centre and r its half-size. D = buoyancy_mass_multiplier + buoyancy_mass_modifier × clamp((m - buoyancy_mass_modifier_lower) ÷ buoyancy_mass_modifier_upper, 0, 1)^buoyancy_mass_modifier_pow. With the defaults 10, 10, 2000, 23000 and 1 this is D = 10 + 10 × clamp((m - 2000) ÷ 23000, 0, 1): D is 10 up to mass 2000 and reaches 20 at 25000, not at 23000. For V = 1 and g = 10 the upward force is 1000 at mass 100, 666.6667 at 13500 and 500 from 25000 on, in internal units. A larger buoyancy_mass_multiplier lowers the force. The force acts at the submerged centroid, so it also makes a torque, and the game adds it to the Bullet force accumulator; it does not set a velocity. Which multiplier applies: the game sets 10 itself and overrides it only from rom/data/game_constants.xml, which this installation does not ship. The SDK copy, also 10, is not on that path. The realtime file's 12 sits in a registry that the release parses but no recovered gameplay code reads, so this build does not use 12. Compartments: a separate loop adds a downward term -g × water_density × 0.01 × (water_compartment_force_factor × W + gas_compartment_force_factor × G) ÷ D. Both factors default to 1 and are missing from the SDK file. W and G are values returned by two fluid compartment getters; G has a stored field ÷ 60 subtracted and is floored at 0. Water drag: the surface callback subtracts 0.5 × the sampled wave velocity from the point velocity, and the vertical part of that term is scaled by 0.3 when it points down (inference: the sampled vector is the wave velocity). With s the relative speed and d the cosine between the flow and the surface normal, a face with d > 0 gets a pressure force A × d^2.5 × (15 s + 17 s²) against its normal and any other face a suction force A × (-d)^0.3 × (12 s + 5 s²) along it, A being the surface weight. Water density does not multiply these two terms. A viscous term opposes motion with viscous_resistance_factor 0.5 × K × 0.00075 × (20 ÷ (s L × 1000000 + 10) + 1.5) × A × water_density × s², L being a body length scalar. K rises from water_drag_factor 1 at mass 2000 to 5 at 25000 (multiplier 4); those two mass thresholds are built into the code and do not follow the buoyancy settings. Partly submerged faces add a slamming term scaled by slamming_force_multiplier 100 and body mass. The sum of the three terms is capped at s × m × 0.5 ÷ 60. The realtime switches apply_drag, apply_viscous_resistance, apply_slamming_force and use_accurate_buoyancy do not occur in the executable; the callback gates its terms by speed and geometry instead.

articles.title: Wheels, grip and suspension
articles.summary: Realtime configuration separates tire damping, suspension stiffness and wheel torque scaling, but the executable contains none of these names; the wheel code uses its own constants.
articles.body: The shipped tuning includes suspension stiffness 0.2 and damping 1, tire stiffness 1 and damping 4, tire_max_friction 100, tire_grip_multiplier 50 and wheel drive torque multiplier 0.0004. None of these seven names occurs in the executable, in ASCII or UTF-16LE, so nothing shows that this build reads them. A native decode of the advanced wheel update (investigation/wheels.md, shown on the Wheels parts pages) found its own constants instead. Units: the working radius r = wheel_radius - 0.125 + 0.125 × wheel_size is in metres, and the tyre surface moves at 2π × r × RPS m/s, 2.199 to 6.597 m/s per RPS for the road wheels at the default wheel_size 1. Speed dependence: the slip velocity between ground and tyre is capped at 5 m/s, so the grip request grows with slip up to 5 m/s and stays flat beyond it. The request is Q = (50 × grip_factor × tyre factor ÷ r) × (2000 q + 100 u), with u the slip and q the contact drift since the last update, at most 0.1 × r and scaled by the brake. The tyre factor is 1, or 1.75 for a double wheel, times 0.25, 0.1875 or 0.125 by tyre type; tank wheels halve it outside a track. Contact: each wheel casts a ray to the ground and also carries a sphere body with Bullet friction 0.001. The contact feeds the shaft: the wheel adds slip ÷ (2π × r) × tyre factor × grip_factor × 0.5 to its RPS and submits that RPS with a weight equal to its definition mass, × 0.7 with suspension. Suspension: the ray spring pushes with 60 × tyre_pressure × (k × max(0, 1.5 × r - l) + c × (l_old - l)), l being the ray distance, k = 0.05 + 0.45 × stiffness_factor and c = 0.5 + 4.5 × damping_factor; wheels without suspension set k and c to 0. Maximum friction: the file's 100 is not a Coulomb limit the code reads. The wheel code's own 100 is the slip gain and the 100 × r slip cap, and the request has no normal-load input. The file's 50 and 4 equal the code's grip scale and tyre damping factor, but the code holds them as built-in numbers.

articles.title: Modular engine assembly and telemetry
articles.summary: Cylinder tooltips describe manifold sharing, and composite output names three data channels.
articles.body: The 1x1 cylinder attaches to a crankshaft and needs manifolds for air, fuel and exhaust. Directly adjacent cylinders can share a manifold according to the supplied tooltip. Cylinder composite values 1, 2 and 3 are air volume, fuel volume and temperature. The starter attaches to a drive belt, and the alternator converts drive belt energy to electric charge. A native decode (investigation/modular-engines.md, shown on the Modular engines parts pages) found how these parts assemble and what the channels hold. Parts joined by crankshaft, belt and cylinder couplings share one crank RPS with inertia I = 1 + the sum of their engine_max_force; parts joined by manifold couplings share one temperature, heat capacity and throttle pair. Each cylinder needs the crank above 2 RPS and its air:fuel ratio inside 12 - 2t to 16 + 4t, with t = manifold °C ÷ 100 clamped to 0 to 1. Its efficiency is a speed factor times 1 - 2 (s - 0.6)², so the best ratio is 13.6 + 0.4t, 13.68 at 20 °C and 14 from 100 °C; the inspected Stoichiometric value 2s - 1 then reads 0.2. An undamaged cylinder adds 80000 × burned fuel × efficiency ÷ I RPS per update, where burned fuel is RPS × 0.000004 × voxels × fuel throttle while the crank is at most 60 RPS and the exhaust has room. Composite value 1 is 6000 × the admitted oxygen, value 2 is 10 × the admitted diesel in litres and value 3 is the manifold temperature in °C. Values 1 and 2 are per cylinder visit, not per second, and value 1 ÷ value 2 is the air:fuel ratio.

articles.title: Speed, altitude and radar signals
articles.summary: Selected sensor descriptions state their units and radar input ranges.
articles.body: Linear speed uses m/s. Angular speed uses rotations per second, and its tooltip names the component y axis. Altitude is metres above sea level. The selected short range radar uses turns for yaw and elevation, with FOV input 0.01 to 0.125 and facing yaw -0.5 to 0.5. Its radar_range field is 5000. That value alone does not guarantee a detection distance for any target. A native decode of the advanced radars (definition type 56: Basic, AWACS, Dish, Phalanx and Missile; investigation/sensors-radio.md, shown on the Other components parts page) found that they also report angles in turns, dividing by 2π. Their working range is R = radar_range × 0.02 × 0.02 ÷ (FOV x × FOV y) on the native FOV fields, a new scan runs every max(1, floor(R ÷ 2000 + 0.5)) updates, and a target passes when its distance is at most R and R ÷ 10000 × signature ÷ distance exceeds 0.025. At the SDK defaults reported distances carry up to ±1% noise and angles up to ±0.001 turn. A later decode (investigation/sensors-legacy.md, shown on the Other components and legacy radar parts pages) found that the signature is the target's physics-body mass, built from the components' definition mass, and that the editor's FOV sliders set each advanced axis from 0.01 to 0.25. It also covers the short range radar here, a legacy type-16 radar: a target passes when signature ÷ distance exceeds 0.25, inside a far plane radar_range × (0.75 + 0.25 × 0.01 ÷ saved radar_fov) ahead, about 3875 m at the saved default 0.1, and inside side planes set by the FOV input. No scan counter precedes its candidate collection, so (inference) it collects on every update that passes its power and height gates. A later static decode (investigation/force-cap.md, shown on the Altimeter and Linear Speed Sensor parts pages) found that the altimeter outputs the part's world Y: height above the fixed sea-level datum y = 0, not clearance over terrain or the local wave surface. It outputs 0 above a height of 40000 or at world X above 156000. The linear speed sensor outputs the physics velocity of its own point, body velocity plus angular velocity × lever arm, in m/s. It does not difference positions, smooth or subtract wind; its four modes give the full speed, the component along its axis, the horizontal speed and the vertical speed. Both are recomputed on every logic update, 60 per simulated second, with no sensor timer of their own. The advanced radar's line-of-sight query filters by collision bits: an object can block only when its collision group lacks bit 0x1000 and shares a bit with 0xff, and its object mask shares a bit with 0x7f. Render materials and transparency take no part in that test.

articles.title: PID controller state and signals
articles.summary: The controller definition says disabling Active resets stored values.
articles.body: The PID takes a measured Process Variable and desired Setpoint, then exposes Control Output. Its Active description explicitly says stored values reset when inactive. The tooltip allows setting proportional, integral and derivative terms with the select tool. The Boolean capacitor is a separate logic component whose signal charges and discharges stored state. A separate native decode of the logic update (investigation/logic.md, shown on the PID Controller parts page) found a per-update recurrence: e = Setpoint - Process Variable, S = S + e, and Control Output = Ki × S + Kp × e + Kd × (e - e_prev) in single precision. There is no time step: at 60 updates per simulated second S gains 60 errors per second, and the derivative is the change over one update. The derivative is 0 on the first active update and has no filter. Turning Active off sets S, the previous error and the output to 0. The physical PID clamps S to ± max_error ÷ max(1e-8, Ki) when max_error is above 0 and turns a NaN or infinite output into 0; it does not limit the output itself. The microprocessor PIDs skip both steps. The capacitor counts whole updates, trunc(60 × charge or discharge time), and its stored charge is a Boolean, so it says nothing about electrical batteries.

articles.title: Base fuel inventory transfers
articles.summary: The storage addon transfers fuel between named vehicle tanks and tile inventories, each port once every 60 onTick callbacks.
articles.body: Storage staggers ports by vehicle ID modulo 60 against a callback counter, so a port is handled on one onTick callback in 60. The counter ignores game_ticks, so the period is 60 callbacks; how long that takes depends on how often the engine calls onTick. Diesel input adds the tank's whole diesel entry to the tile inventory, with no per-callback limit, then requests 0 fresh water and 0 nitrogen in the inlet. Jet input does the same with the jet fuel entry. Diesel output computes the free space as capacity minus the tank's total value, clamps it to the tile's diesel stock, subtracts that delta from the stock and requests old total plus delta of the tank's current dominant fluid_type, then 0 nitrogen. Jet output does the same with jet fuel. Inputs run before outputs, so fuel credited by an inlet can leave through an outlet in the same callback. Example: an outlet of capacity 100 holding 40 with 25 in stock requests 65 and leaves 0 in stock. The output request keeps the tank's existing fluid_type, so a diesel outlet holding mostly jet fuel debits diesel stock while asking for more of the jet fuel; the input clears fresh water and nitrogen, not the fuel it credited. A native decode (investigation/small-parts.md) found that server.setVehicleTank does not write the tank itself. Its binding resolves the named tank and appends a 36-byte request, kind 2, holding the vehicle ID, voxel position, value and fluid ID, to a queue; the tank changes only when that queue is applied. This is addon bookkeeping rather than the fluid network solver.

articles.title: Jet startup, turbines and afterburners
articles.summary: Jet component descriptions separate electrical startup, combustion and exhaust controls.
articles.body: The compressor requires electrical power to begin compression. The combustion chamber takes jet fuel and throttle from 0 to 1, and its tooltip says combustion begins when internal pressure is high enough without giving a threshold. Turbines convert air pressure to RPS. The medium turbine documents a torque connection for motor startup or driving props and generators. The afterburner adds thrust at increased fuel consumption. Its thrust spoiler input runs from 0 for no reduction to 1 for total reduction. The separate Turbine Engine part (turbine.xml) is not a jet part: a native decode (investigation/classic-engines.md) found it runs the classic diesel engine update, so its engine_max_force of 100000 says nothing about jet turbines. A native decode of the modular jet update (investigation/jet-engines.md, shown on the Jet engines parts pages) found that combustion needs internal RPS strictly above 0.5, not a pressure threshold. The effective throttle u is clamped to 0 to 1 and limited by the jet fuel in the chamber, which burns 0.12 × u × RPS L/s. The compressor, enabled and powered, requests 0.1 charge per update, transfers 0.2 × (100 × r0 - (p_out - p_in)) of pressure state and loses 0.0001 times that transfer in RPS after its starter input and 0.99 retention. Combustion adds 1600 × u × RPS pressure and 0.1 × u × RPS internal temperature per update. Turbines halve the incoming pressure, gain 0.0000375 × pressure RPS when undamaged and charge their Electric connection. The power connection of the medium turbine submits its RPS with shaft weight 160. Exhaust force is 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000), scaled by altitude, the thrust spoiler and an afterburner multiplier of 1 + 500 × the jet fuel stored in the exhaust, and capped at 100 × S, S being the summed adjusted mass of the bodies joined by joints (investigation/force-cap.md). RPS reaches the exhaust only through the pressure the chamber adds. The exhaust branch never subtracts jet fuel; its Fuel port exchanges with the pipe network separately.

articles.title: Fireboxes, boilers and condensers
articles.summary: A firebox burns at most 0.00002 × voxels coal per update and heats its coolant; boilers and condensers convert water and steam at a fixed temperature of 100, at min(0.001 × (T - 100), water) per update when boiling.
articles.body: The coal firebox consumes one coal to ignite and provides air, exhaust and coolant connections. The boiler tooltip recommends a firebox heat supply and controlling evaporation to maintain consistent output steam pressure. Its labelled Water In and Steam Out ports have no descriptions. The condenser converts steam back to water and should be continuously cooled; its coolant descriptions explicitly call for cold fluid. A native decode (investigation/steam.md, shown on the Steam parts pages) found that the firebox requests 0.00002 × voxels × clamp((600 - T) ÷ 400, 0, 1) coal per update, at most 0.054 and 0.21 per simulated second for the small and large firebox. It burns only while Air pressure is more than 1 above Exhaust pressure and oxygen covers the request at a 0.21 reference fraction, and each unit of coal burned adds 200 to the fire temperature. The fire loses 0.001 of its gap to the surroundings per update and exchanges heat with its coolant at k = 0.0008 × voxels, the fire weighted 400. Boilers and condensers convert in their phase chamber at a fixed temperature of 100, whatever the pressure: at or above 100, min(0.001 × (T - 100), water) per update becomes steam, 1:1 by stored amount; below 100, min(0.001 × (100 - T), 0.1 × steam) condenses. Phase and coolant chambers exchange heat at k = 0.1 × (1 - D), D = clamp(0.1 × damage, 0, 1), weighted by liquid amount, and lose 0.0001 of their gap to the surroundings per update. Boiler Water In admits fresh water one way in with bias -60, and Steam Out passes steam one way out with bias 2.5 × steam ÷ phase volume; the condenser's Steam In and Water Out are the reverse with no bias, and the coolant ports enforce no direction. The port solver's 0 to 60 target clamp is a flow rule, not a pressure limit, and the boiler, condenser and phase code contain no pressure limit or burst test.

articles.title: Steam turbines and piston timing
articles.summary: The turbine turns steam flow into a target RPS that keeps 0.985 per update; the piston switches its own ports at half turn and drives its crank by 0.002 × steam pressure difference × sin(2πz).
articles.body: The turbine tooltip says torque comes from the force generated by steam passing through it. Its Steam In, Steam Out and RPS ports are labels without descriptions. The piston tooltip says outer-coupling pressure extends the piston and inner-coupling pressure retracts it. Alternating pressure according to piston position allows the crankpin to rotate continuously. The piston also has labelled Piston Position and RPS signals and two described power connections. A native decode (investigation/steam.md, shown on the Steam parts pages) found that the turbine passes gas one way from Steam In to Steam Out through the pump solver with flow factor 0.0025, so exhaust pressure at or above inlet pressure stops it, and it consumes no steam. Each update its speed gains 1000 × the steam moved, is multiplied by 0.985 and is submitted as target RPS with shaft weight 65 on each RPS port; unloaded it settles at 0.985 ÷ 0.015 × 1000 × the steam moved per update. The piston's crank phase z runs 0 to 1 turns and is the Piston Position output. Each chamber has a Steam In and a Steam Out, and the update opens one of each pair by half turn, switching at z = 0.5, so no external valve timing is needed. Each update it adds 0.002 × (p_B - p_A) × sin(2πz) to its crank group, p being chamber pressure times steam fraction, and submits the group speed with shaft weight 20 × voxels per port. The render crank radii 0.075, 0.146 and 0.216 suggest strokes of 0.15, 0.292 and 0.432 world units (inference).

articles.title: Nuclear fuel assemblies and control rods
articles.summary: Fuel assemblies add the reactions of up to four coupled fuel assemblies, control rods scale the excess over 0.1 × fuel by 1 − 0.01 × insertion, and fuel rods heat by 0.1 × r per update and take damage above 1500.
articles.body: A fuel rod can be inserted into a fuel assembly to begin fission. The assembly tooltip says fuel rods consume uranium ingots from workbench inventory to fuel. A control rod decreases the reaction rate of adjacent rods. The assembly labels Release Fuel Rod and Fuel Rod Temperature, while the control rod labels Insertion Target and Insertion; their port descriptions are empty. A native decode (investigation/nuclear.md, shown on the Nuclear parts pages) names the three nuclear_component_type values from the editor selector: 0 fuel assembly, 1 fuel rod and 2 control rod. Each update an assembly with a rod computes A = b + 0.999 × (R − b), B = S + 0.998 × (A − S) and b + (1 − 0.01 × C) × (B − b), with b = 0.1 × fuel fraction, R the rod's reaction, S the summed reaction of coupled fuel assemblies and C the summed insertion of coupled control rods; the rod then clamps its reaction r to 0 to 50. Adjacency is the four control_rod couplings x+, x-, z+ and z-, not a radius, so an assembly sees at most four neighbours, fuel or control. Insertion follows Insertion Target clamped to 0 to 1 by at most 0.005 per update, 200 updates or 3.333 s for a full stroke; larger insertion lowers the reaction but never below the 0.1 × fuel baseline. A rod uses 1e-8 × r of its fuel per update, so a full rod lasts 33333 s, 9.259 simulated hours, at r = 50. It heats by 0.1 × r per update, exchanges heat with immersed coolant at k = 0.001 × (q ÷ A) × w, the rod counting as 100 liquid amount and its own step capped at 0.5, and moves 0.001 of the way to its surroundings. A rod above r = 0.001 is a live radiation source of strength s = 0.1 × r with linear falloff over 10 × s metres, cut by 200 m across compartments, and assemblies add 0.001 × reaction ÷ A to their coolant's contamination, which a radiation detector inside reads. Strictly above 1500 a rod takes damage at once and then every 300 hot updates, up to 50; the update has no separate meltdown or explosion temperature.

articles.title: Gear ratios and clutch engagement
articles.summary: Gearboxes pull RPS B toward the selected ratio × RPS A, so for N:1 the A side is fast; the standalone clutch couples with strength input^6 and the modular clutch follows input^3 with a slew.
articles.body: The selected gearbox definitions expose power connections A and B, an electrical connection and a Gear Switch input. Their tooltips say the switch toggles between two property values. The torque_gearbox_2 tooltip states an operating torque difference up to 4000 without specifying a unit. The standard clutch takes engagement from 0 to 1 and says this controls transmitted power. The modular clutch attaches to a crankshaft to control torque made available to the connected system. A native decode (investigation/transmission.md, shown on the Transmission parts pages) found that every gearbox offers the same eight ratios: 1:-1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1, as multipliers q = -1, 1, 5/6, 2/3, 5/9, 1/2, 2/5 and 1/3. The gearbox stores q on RPS A and 1 ÷ q on RPS B, and the shaft solver pulls RPS B toward q × RPS A, so for an N:1 option RPS A is the fast side and RPS B targets A ÷ N. The two sides stay separate shaft groups. Each update a group adds the other side's speed with path weight h = 0.95 × c, where c is 1 for an intact gearbox, adding sign(q) × v × I × h to its numerator and I × h ÷ |q| to its weight; paths with h at or below 0.001 add nothing. This is a weighted speed exchange with no slip threshold, and 0.95 is not a 95% power efficiency: two groups already at the ratio stay there. Gear Switch picks Ratio Off or Ratio On, and a new ratio replaces the old one in the same update while the gearbox has any electrical availability; without power it keeps the last ratio and stays coupled. The standalone clutch sets c = e × clamp(input, 0, 1)^6 directly each update, with e = min(1, availability ÷ 0.01), so input 0.5 gives 1/64 and an isolated clutch transfers nothing below about 0.319. The modular clutch is separate code: its engagement moves toward clamp(input, 0, 1)^3 by at most 0.1 per update. Nonzero damage sets a gearbox's or standalone clutch's coupling to 0. The gearbox force_emitter_max_force values (200, 1200 and 5000; 1000 and 9999999 for the legacy definitions) are copied at binding but not used as a solver weight, so they are not torque capacities.

articles.title: Underwater propellers and pitch control
articles.summary: Marine propellers push only with the hub at or below the water surface, and pitch is a normalized -1 to 1 value in a decoded RPS and flow law.
articles.body: The small boat propeller receives engine power and its tooltip says it operates only underwater. The controllable-pitch boat propeller also requires underwater operation and takes desired pitch from -1 to 1. Its force_emitter_max_force field is 80000 versus 20000 for the selected small fixed-pitch propeller. A native decode (investigation/propulsion.md, shown on the Propulsion parts pages) found that every propeller, rotor and ducted fan runs one force-emitter update. Each update it scales the published shaft speed by 0.9999 to w, forms the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + Pitch input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × intact blades × 0.32, where U is minus the hub's velocity through still water along the thrust axis, signed by the pitch. With K = force_emitter_max_force ÷ 1000, or F × intact blades ÷ 8000 for the pitchable propellers, q = clamp(b ÷ 2K, -10, 10) is multiplied by 10 below the water surface; the propeller removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its shaft and pushes with 1500 × K × removed RPS, signed by the pitch, in the game's internal force unit. Thrust is queued only when the hub is at or below the sampled water surface; the shaft load applies either way. force_emitter_max_force is therefore a solver weight, not a thrust ceiling: at 10 RPS and pitch 1 the small fixed propeller gives about 22201 internal force, and the small, standard and large pitchable propellers about 4074, 20411 and 35002 per RPS. Pitch is a normalized number, not a blade angle; zero pitch gives no load and no thrust. A separate application cap of 100 × S limits the force actually applied.

articles.title: Aircraft propellers and rotor controls
articles.summary: Rotor and propeller inputs are normalized pitch and cyclic values in a decoded thrust, shaft-load and force-geometry law.
articles.body: The aircraft propeller takes collective from -1 to 1, and its tooltip links thrust to received engine torque without giving an equation. The selected large helicopter rotor has roll, pitch and collective inputs from -1 to 1. Its tooltip describes pitch and roll control through the swashplate and says force decreases underwater. The tail rotor takes yaw from -1 to 1 to control generated force. A native decode (investigation/propulsion.md, shown on the Propulsion parts pages) found one force-emitter update for all of them. The effective pitch is clamp(saved pitch + Collective, -1, 1), a normalized number, not degrees or turns; the saved pitch starts at force_emitter_default_pitch, 1 for the main rotors and the aircraft propeller and 0 for the tail rotor, so Collective -1 gives zero thrust on a main rotor and the tail rotor's Yaw is a signed pitch. From the shaft speed, pitch and air-relative flow the part computes a load b, removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its shaft with q = clamp(b ÷ 2K, -10, 10), and pushes with 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency, where K = force_emitter_max_force ÷ 1000 or ÷ 2000 with 4 intact blades. Roll and Pitch move the force point by -4 × input along local X and Z and tilt its direction by 0.4 × input. Thrust is scaled by (1 - 2.2413793e-5 × altitude)^5.3595023, 0 above 40000. With the hub below the water surface the scalar update gives no thrust and multiplies q by 10, so the rotor brakes its shaft; that is the decreased underwater force. A physical rotor hinge gets a motor with impulse limit 1000, and coaxial rotors add an opposing force pair of 800 × b × clamp(|pitch + Collective + 0.1|, 0, 1) about the rotor axis.

articles.title: Weapon loading, ammunition and timed fuses
articles.summary: Guns fire at a fixed muzzle speed per weapon class, barrel length sets only the muzzle position, and loading runs on per-class breech and receiver timers; Fuse Timer detonates fragmentation rounds, and high-explosive rounds from the heavy autocannon up, at an interpolated point.
articles.body: The light autocannon trigger feeds, loads and fires cartridges from connected belts or drums. Its tooltip requires electricity for loading. The selected small drum has weapon_ammo_capacity 100, reports ammo count and cannot mix calibers. Feeder belts use electrical power to transfer cartridges in the arrow direction. The battle cannon trigger fires a loaded shell, and Open Breech permits loading. Its optional Fuse Timer is explicitly in seconds for high-explosive and fragmentation ammunition. A native decode (investigation/weapons.md, shown on the Weapons parts pages) found that weapon_class selects one of seven gun records. Muzzle speed is 800, 1000, 1000, 900, 800, 700 and 600 m/s for the machine gun, light, rotary and heavy autocannon, battle, artillery and Bertha cannon, added to the firing body's velocity; weapon_barrel_length_voxels only places the muzzle, at 0.175 + 0.25 per voxel of the gun and each barrel extension or muzzle brake. Each update a round moves by velocity ÷ 60, loses 0.5 × (138750 ÷ (138750 + height))² m/s of vertical speed, 30 m/s² at sea level, and keeps 0.975, 0.98, 0.99, 0.995, 0.998, 0.999 or 0.9995 of its velocity; in water the step is 0.2 and the retention × 0.8. Rounds are removed after 300 updates from the machine gun and the light and rotary autocannon, 600 from the heavy autocannon and 3600 from the cannons, and machine-gun and autocannon rounds are also removed below 50 m/s. Spread is two independent angles within ±0.25 × dispersion × m radians, dispersion 0.01, 0.02 for the rotary autocannon and 0.005 for artillery and Bertha, and each barrel extension lowers m by 0.2 to at least 0.5 without changing muzzle speed. Impact magnitude is B × speed ÷ 1000 for kinetic rounds, × 0.4 for armour-piercing and × 0.65 for incendiary, and B or 0.4 × B for high explosive or fragmentation, with B from 0.1 to 4; explosions search within 7.5 × that magnitude in metres. Armour-piercing rounds lose 100 × p × mass ÷ cells of speed per struck cell. Breech transitions take 2, 4, 1, 16, 75, 250 and 600 updates and the battle, artillery and Bertha receivers wait 30, 90 and 240 updates after a round arrives, the heavy autocannon 6. Inferred from that state machine, the automatic guns cycle at most at 900, 450, 1800 and about 94.7 rounds per minute. Drums hold their weapon_ammo_capacity of light rounds, half in rotary rounds and a fifth in heavy rounds. Fuse Timer applies to fragmentation rounds, and to high-explosive rounds on the heavy autocannon and the cannons: T = max(1/60, input + 0.02 × u - 0.01) s with u random from 0 to 1, and the round detonates in the update where (age + 1) ÷ 60 reaches T, interpolated within that update.

articles.title: Composite data over electrical cables
articles.summary: A composite value is 32 on/off channels and 32 binary32 numbers, numbered 1 to 32, in 132 bytes. Wires, microprocessor bridges and Electrical Cable Anchors copy it whole, and anchors also pass a video descriptor and a private copy of the audio samples.
articles.body:
The electrical cable anchor tooltip permits one rope logic link between two anchors, carrying data and electricity. Its ports are composite, on/off, video and audio send and receive pairs. A native check (investigation/config.md) of the scalar input getter 0x1408cacf0 found that it copies a cached value and returns, so reading an input does not evaluate the upstream graph.

A native decode (investigation/composite.md, shown on the Electrical Cable Anchor, Microprocessor and Logic pages) recovered the value and every copy of it. The value starts with a 32-bit on/off mask, channel c at bit c - 1, followed by 32 numbers, channel c at byte 4 × c, so channel 32 starts at byte 128. Lua getBool and getNumber return false and 0 outside 1 to 32. This is the in-memory value, not a network or save format.

Table: Composite value
| Part | Where | Channel c |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On/off mask | 32-bit word at byte 0 | bit c - 1 |
| Numbers | 32 binary32 values from byte 4 | byte 4 × c |

Wires: the dispatcher first runs every component update, then goes through the vehicles one at a time. For each vehicle it runs the transport pass, which holds the cable copy, and then flushes that vehicle's outputs: each output pushes its value into the cache of every input wired to it. Inference: on an ordinary wire a consumer reads a new value one update after the producer wrote it.

Cables: an anchor reads its linked peer and, while both states are below 5, copies its Composite Input value, all 132 bytes, to the peer's Composite Output, its on/off input to the peer's On/Off Output, its video descriptor to the peer's Video Data Receive and its audio samples to the peer's Audio Data Receive. Video is copied by value with no allocation; audio goes into a buffer the receiving anchor owns. Electric Cable Pulleys (subtype 9) route the same copies through their own buffers. Because cable copies and output flushes interleave vehicle by vehicle, a write to an anchor on another vehicle can land before or after that vehicle's flush, so the number of updates a cable adds depends on vehicle order.

Microcontrollers: composite bridges copy the whole value, video bridges the descriptor and audio bridges the samples. The editor limits width and length to 1 to 6, and upload rejects anything above 6.

articles.title: Winch controls, length and hose connections
articles.summary: Winch descriptions document electrical operation, length telemetry and hose-coil ports. Rope-node winches reel at 0.012 × cable_length × Speed m/s; legacy winches and the Hose reel at 0.24 × Speed m/s at full electricity.
articles.body: The selected mechanical winch raises its cable on Up and lowers it on Down. Length reports the current cable length in metres. The selected large variant documents the same controls and units. Their short tooltips describe 20m and 100m mechanical winches respectively. Both expose electrical and hose-coil fluid connections. A native decode (investigation/winches.md, shown on the winch, Hose and winch end parts pages) found two reel implementations. Rope-node winches (type 48, Small, Medium, Large and Huge at 10, 40, 150 and 600 m) step the rope by 0.0002 × cable_length × Speed metres per update: 0.12, 0.48, 1.8 and 7.2 m/s at the default Speed 1, editor range 0.1 to 10. Both ends of a rope share one limit, the sum of their cable_length values, and a step is kept only while the length stays above 0.1 m and below that sum, so a step that would cross a bound is dropped rather than clamped. A Speed input from -1 to 1 replaces the buttons at a magnitude of 0.1 or more. Holding both buttons cancels. After each accepted step the winch requests 0.01 charge units (0.6 per second); the reply does not scale the step, and with no usable electricity the buttons are ignored. Static inference: the Speed input bypasses that gate. Legacy winches (type 20: Small, Medium, Large and Huge at 10, 20, 100 and 500 m) and the 16 m Hose step by 0.004 × Speed × p metres per update, p being the supplied fraction of a 0.01 charge request made for each held control: 0.24 m/s at Speed 1 and full supply for every size, editor range 0.1 to 5. Their rest length is clamped to 0.25 m to cable_length, both inclusive. Holding both controls cancels at full supply and costs two requests; under shortage Up is served first, so the rope shortens. The winch end pieces are the far attachment and fluid end of their winch, with no reel of their own; all five end-piece files are identical, and the Large and Huge Winches both use winch_b. Hose coils and rope hoses link the two fluid networks without a length term, so a longer cable adds no hose volume or flow loss (Hose and winch part articles).

articles.title: Magnetic connectors, transfers and hardpoints
articles.summary: Connector tooltips specify attachment conditions and distinguish release from launch. Small, fluid, electric, torque and hardpoint connectors attach under 0.5 m between centres, hinge and large connectors under 0.25 m with their samples lined up; magnet_force scales only the pull before attaching.
articles.body: Small magnetic connectors require proximity and both magnets switched on. Electric and fluid connector tooltips describe attachment by proximity and free transfer of their respective resources when connected. Torque connectors document mechanical-energy transfer. These connectors report attachment and expose composite and video send/receive ports. Hardpoint bodies require correct alignment and transfer logic and fluid. Release disconnects; Launch also activates the attached ordnance, with a Launched output on the attachment. A native decode (investigation/connectors.md, shown on the connector, hardpoint and Mag All part pages) gives the rules. A connector searches 10 m for a partner of the same connector_type, or the other half of a hardpoint pair. Small, fluid, electric and torque connectors and hardpoints attach when the centres are under 0.5 m apart, hinge and large connectors under 0.25 m. Large, hinge and hardpoint connectors also need each of their samples (four rim points, two axis endpoints or two axial points, 0.25 m from the centre) within 0.1118 m of a partner sample. Before attaching, small, hinge and large connectors pull each update with F = 60 × magnet_force × P × W × d ÷ (1 + |d|²) for offsets under 1 m, P being the electrical supply factor and W the lighter body's native weight field; rim and endpoint samples pull at gain 0.15. Fluid, electric, torque and hardpoint connectors carry definition flag 0x100000, which removes the pull and makes their Release input start a 120-update (2 s) detach that holding the input keeps restarting. Attached pairs are held by a Bullet joint: point-to-point for small, fluid, electric and torque connectors, hinge for hinge connectors, fixed for large connectors and hardpoints. Its break threshold is the largest double and the attach routine never reads magnet_force, so magnet_force (0.1, 0.15, 0.2) is not a holding force. While linked, each update copies the composite signal (32 on/off channels and 32 numbers), on/off and number signals and the video source straight to the partner, with no buffer or averaging. Fluid moves between the two networks through the two-port solver at factor 0.5 and bias 0; electric connectors and hardpoints join their electrical networks into one charge pool; large and torque connectors link their shaft nodes. A hardpoint attachment sends its ordnance type code to the body's Ordinance Type output: 1 Utility, 2 Fuel, 3 Unguided bomb, 4 Laser Guided Bomb, 5 GPS Guided Bomb, 6 Rocket, 7 Rocket Pod, 8 Laser Guided Missile, 9 GPS Guided Missile, 10 Radar Guided Missile, 11 Torpedo, 12 Cannon. Launch sets a latch on the attachment, output as Launched, and detaches it like Release. The Mag All grabs whatever touches a 0.125 m contact sphere with a point-to-point joint. Its Force output is the joint's absolute solver impulse in internal units, and it lets go above 200 × the electrical supply factor, then waits 30 updates.
